Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City OFFICE OF THE UNDERSECRETARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT 01 June 2009 PUNONG BARANGAY NAPOLEON T. TANDOG Barangay oblacion San Jose, omblon Dear PB Tandog: Thi has reference to your earlier letter addressed to DILG Assistant Provincial Director Danton Arevalo, that Province, asking for a legal opinion r garding Administrative Case No. 2008-03 for Oppression and Abuse of uthority filed against you by Edison Manuel before the Office of the Sang uniang Bayan in San Jose, Romblon. DILG Region IV-B Director Rolando Rafael forwarded said letter to this level. An xamination of the documents attached to your letter reveals that the Sangg niang Bayan has already came up with Resolution No. 12, series of 2009 d ted 17 March 2009 embodying the Decision in your case. The Decision tated in its dispositive portion that the Sangguniang Bayan found yo guilty of the administrative offense of Oppression and Abuse of Authority and sentenced you to suffer a suspension for six (6) months without p y effective upon receipt of a copy thereof. In our letter, you said that in conducting the proceedings of your case and n the contents of the Decision itself, you observed and in fact, specifical enumerated therein the alleged irregular/inconsistent acts committe by the Sangguniang Bayan. Thus, you are now seeking this Departme t's legal opinion for a clearer explanation on the matter. In ply thereto, please be informed that we are constrained from rendering a legal opinion on the matter. Since the Sangguniang Bayan has already r dered a Decision in your case as embodied in its Resolution No. 12, series of 2009 dated 17 March 2009, any question as to the irregularities in the pr ceedings conducted by that body or on the invalidity of the

-2- Decision itself is already a proper subject of an administrative appeal filed before the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. Your remedy therefore is not to seek for legal opinion from this Department but to file an appeal pursuant to Section 67 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160), thus: "Section 67. Adminis trative Appeals . - Decisions in administrative cases may, within thirty (30) days from receipt thereof, be appealed to the following: (a) The sangguniang panlalawigan, in the case of decisions of the sangguniang panlungsod of component cities and the sangguniang bayan;" In ne of the follow-ups made, it was represented that you already filed an ppeal before the Sangguniang Panlalawigan in accordance with the afor uoted provision but that August Body, unfortunately, has taken no action thereto up to this date. The matter is already within the domain of that Aug st Body. Accordingly, we suggest that you file a Motion for Early Resolutio of your appeal before the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. This Departm t cannot, in exercising its general supervisory power over local governm nt units, pre-empt or interfere with the Sangguniang Panlalawi an's disposition of the appeal by rendering an opinion on the issue. Mo over, in the 2nd Indorsement of Dir. Rafael, it is represented that Mayor Fil ino T. Tandog of San Jose, Romblon has not yet implemented the Decis n of the Sangguniang Bayan on the case at hand. In this regard, may we i vite your attention to Section 68 of the Local Government Code of 1991, t us: "SECTION 68. Execution Pending Appeal. - An appeal Sha not prevent a decision from becoming final or executory. The respondent shall be considered as having been placed under preventive suspension during the pendency of an app al in the event he wins such appeal. In the event the app al results in an exoneration, he shall be paid his salary and such other emoluments during the pendency of the app al." Bas d on the foregoing, the decision of the Sangguniang Bayan shall imm diately be final and executory upon receipt of a copy thereof by

-3- the respondent and an appeal shall not prevent a decision from becoming final and executory. While it may be conceded that the filing of an appeal or even a motion for reconsideration ordinarily stays the execution of a decision appealed from, this does not, however, apply to administrative disciplinary actions against local elective officials. This is evident from the language of Section 68, as aforequoted. We hope that we have addressed your concern accordingly. Very truly yours, Encl: cc: AUSTERE A.
